name: Capsule generation, demo run
source: Flow focusing: Anna SL, Bontoux N, Stone HA. Appl Phys Lett 2003;82:364, doi:10.1063/1.1537519. Design rules relating orifice, flows and droplet size: Lashkaripour A et al., Nat Commun 2021;12:25, doi:10.1038/s41467-020-20284-z. Core-shell semipermeable capsules by aqueous two-phase separation inside the droplet: Leonaviciene G & Mazutis L, Nucleic Acids Res 2023;51:e2, doi:10.1093/nar/gkac918.
description: The demo: prime, start the streams, settle the junction, film the droplet train, collect and cure. About 213 capsules of 390 um from a 300 um nozzle in roughly 35 min on a 30 x 20 mm single-depth chip. The streams keep the full module's oil-to-aqueous ratio, but their total is set by the delay line's shear ceiling (0.01 dyn/cm2 in delay_1), so it runs slower than the full module; droplet size follows the nozzle and the flow ratio rather than the size of the board. The batch is what fits in 10 min at that rate. Reagent names are generic; see the source citation.

steps.note: Prime the board with oil before anything aqueous goes in. Do this first and always: the walls have to be oil-wetted for water-in-oil to work at all, and an aqueous stream that touches a dry wall first will wet it and keep wetting it.

Start the two aqueous streams and the oil, and let the junction settle. Expect a minute or two of ragged, uneven droplets before it locks into a steady drip: that is normal, and it is the syringe pump and the tubing settling rather than the chip. Cells ride in the core stream at about 13 cells/uL, which gives a mean of 0.2 cells per capsule. That figure belongs to a 390 um capsule and falls as the cube of diameter, so do not reuse it if the nozzle changes. At about 0.36 droplets per second the demo batch of 213 capsules takes about 10 min.

FILM THIS. The serpentine shows a regular train of 390 um capsules. Even spacing and even size is the whole result: if droplets vary in size the flow ratio is off, and if they merge the surfactant or the surface treatment is wrong.

Collect into a tube on ice. Let the two aqueous polymers demix for a few minutes, which is what puts the shell on the outside, then flood-cure at 405 nm. Curing is off-chip on purpose: demixing takes minutes, and a serpentine holding minutes at this flow would be longer than the board.
